trial_court: Family Court, Manipur at Lamphelpat, Imphal West in Mat. (Divorce) Suit No. 68 of 2015
case_name: Smt. Phijam (N) Khwairakpam (O) Babina ... vs Khwairakpam Ragesh Singh

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Phijam (N) Khwairakpam (O) Babina Devi, wife/defendant No.1

facts_of_case: The parties were married on 03-02-2014 and the husband returned home in July 2014, taking back the wife to his place of posting. The trial court dissolved the marriage with a direction to pay permanent alimony of Rs. 2,00,000/- to the wife.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse's moral obligation to maintain the other spouse is a relevant consideration in determining alimony.
legal_principles.held: Taking into consideration the moral obligation on the part of the plaintiff who is the husband of the defendant No.1, it is further ordered that the plaintiff is to pay a sum of Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees two lakh only) as permanent alimony within the period of 8 months from the date of passing this judgment and order.

legal_principles.principle: A court may consider the mental agony suffered by a spouse in determining alimony.
legal_principles.held: to compensate the mental agony the defendant has to go through after separation from her husband forever.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is partly allowed and the impugned order dated 06-07-2019 passed by the Ld. Family Court is set aside, and the matter is remitted back to the trial court for fresh disposal.

keywords: Latin maxim: 'Nemo dat quod non habet'
